text:
Carefully tuned to

the song of a fish

I was in the kitchen

halfway to madness

dreaming of Hemingway’s

Spain.

It’s muggy, as they say,

I can’t breathe,

I have shit and

read the sports pages,

I opened the refrigerator,

saw a piece of purple

meat

and put it back

there.

The place to find the center

is at the edge

that rattling in the sky

is only a pipe

vibrating.

Terrible things advance along the

walls; cancer flowers grow

on the porch; my white cat

had one eye torn out

and there are only 7 days left

of racing

in the summer season.

The dancer never came from the

Normandy Club

and Jimmy didn’t bring the

whore,

but there is a postcard from

Arkansas

and a returnable form from Food King:

10 free days in Hawaii,

all you have to do

is fill it out

but I don’t want to go to

Hawaii

I want the whore with pelican eyes

bronze navel

and

ivory heart.

I take out the piece of purple

meat,

throw it into the

pan.

Then the telephone rings.

I fall to one knee

and roll under

the table. I stay there

until it stops ringing.

Then I get up and

turn on

the radio.

No wonder Hemingway was

a drunk, goddamned Spain!

I can’t stand it

either.

It’s so terribly

muggy.
